# 01 · POV: mom spots the slouch

**Pillar:** A · **Length:** 12–20 s · **Hook type:** POV / self-identification

**Use when:** You have a kid, a couch and 10 minutes. The reliable weekly banker.

## Structure (beats)
[0–1.5 s] Static shot of kid folded over the iPad, text 'POV: you look over and see this'. [1.5–6 s] Mom reaction (dead stare / sigh), no words. [6–12 s] Hand enters, pops the DigiRoo stand up, screen rises, kid sits up without being told. [12–18 s] Same framing, kid upright, text 'and now I don't have to say sit up'. CTA line.

## Script skeleton
```
(spoken, optional, can be text-only)
'Every parent has seen this.' [slouch]
'Nobody wants to say sit up fifteen times.' [reaction]
'So the screen comes up instead.' [lift]
'DigiRoo. It's in my bio.'
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Kid slouched, phone static on a chair, waist-level, 5 s
2. Mom face reaction, selfie angle, 3 s
3. Hands + case: stand lifts, same angle as shot 1, 5 s
4. Kid upright, same angle as shot 1, 5 s (match framing exactly for the before/after feel)

## On-screen text pattern
POV: you look over and see this → and now I don't have to say 'sit up'

## Why it works
Instant self-identification; before/after inside one framing; zero talking needed so it works with any trending sound.

## How DigiRoo uses it
Rotate the setting weekly: couch, car seat, restaurant, grandma's, airplane tray.

# 02 · Before/after in 7 seconds

**Pillar:** C · **Length:** 7–12 s · **Hook type:** Visual anomaly / reveal

**Use when:** You need a quick product post and have 2 clips. Great for Stories and ads later.

## Structure (beats)
[0–3 s] 'Before': kid hunched, head down, text 'iPad neck'. Hard cut. [3–7 s] 'After': stand up, screen at eye level, kid upright, text 'DigiRoo'. [7–10 s] Hold + CTA.

## Script skeleton
```
(no voice; sound + text only)
Text 1: 'tablet neck'  Text 2: 'tablet neck, elevated'
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Side profile of kid with iPad flat, 4 s
2. Same side profile with DigiRoo raised, 4 s
3. Optional: slow hand lift transition, 3 s

## On-screen text pattern
before → after → 'Screen Time, Elevated.'

## Why it works
Side profile makes the head angle undeniable; short enough to loop, which boosts completion rate.

## How DigiRoo uses it
Film every before/after from the side at kid-head height. Loop-friendly: end on the same frame you started on.

# 03 · Chiropractor explains tech neck in 20 s

**Pillar:** B · **Length:** 20–30 s · **Hook type:** Credential + problem callout

**Use when:** Pillar B week; you have a clinician quote (or an affiliate willing to be on camera / voice note).

## Structure (beats)
[0–2 s] 'A pediatric chiropractor told me the one thing she wishes parents knew about tablets.' [2–10 s] The point, in plain words: the lower the screen, the further the head drops, the more load on the neck. Show the angle with a hand gesture or a kid profile. [10–20 s] 'The habit fix': bring the screen up. Demo. [20–28 s] 'Not medical advice, just the thing that worked at our house.' CTA.

## Script skeleton
```
'A pediatric chiropractor told me the one thing she wishes parents knew about tablets.'
'It's not the screen time. It's the screen height.'
'When the screen's in their lap, the head goes down and stays down.'
'Bring the screen up to eye level and the neck comes with it.'
'That's the whole reason I made DigiRoo. Link's in the bio.'
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Antonia to camera, selfie, 6 s
2. Kid profile slouched, 4 s
3. Hand gesture showing head angle OR drawn arrow overlay, 4 s
4. Stand raised, kid upright, 6 s
5. Antonia to camera for CTA, 4 s

## On-screen text pattern
'it's not the screen time… it's the screen height' / 'eye level' / [REVIEW: clinician]

## Why it works
Borrowed authority without medical claims; keyword-dense (tech neck, pediatric chiropractor, screen time) for search; clinicians share it because it makes them look good.

## How DigiRoo uses it
Always flag for review. Never name a clinician who hasn't agreed. Reuse as the first post in the affiliate content pack.

# 04 · Unboxing with a kid

**Pillar:** C · **Length:** 25–40 s · **Hook type:** Demo cold-open

**Use when:** You have a sealed unit and a kid who'll react. Also the easiest UGC brief for affiliates and customers.

## Structure (beats)
[0–2 s] Kid's hands tearing the box, text 'she's been waiting for this'. [2–12 s] Pull out, colour reaction, iPad goes in. [12–25 s] Kid discovers the stand: lifts, tilts, sets it on the floor/table, sits up. [25–35 s] Kid verdict (one unscripted line). CTA.

## Script skeleton
```
(mostly unscripted; prompts)
Mom: 'What do you think it does?'
Kid: …
Mom: 'Try pulling that up.'
Kid: …
Mom: 'Where would you use it?'
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Top-down of box opening, 5 s
2. Kid face reaction, 3 s
3. Hands fitting the iPad, 5 s
4. Kid finding the stand, side angle, 8 s
5. Kid using it, wide, 5 s
6. Kid's one-liner, 4 s

## On-screen text pattern
'she's been waiting for this' / 'wait for the stand' / kid quote as caption

## Why it works
Kids' genuine reactions are the highest-trust UGC; the stand reveal is a built-in 'wait for it'.

## How DigiRoo uses it
Save the kid's unscripted line; it becomes next week's hook. Send this exact shot list to affiliates and customers as the UGC brief.

# 05 · Stitch / react to the stat

**Pillar:** B · **Length:** 15–25 s · **Hook type:** Pattern interrupt / reaction

**Use when:** A news clip, study or creator video about kids' screen time or tech neck is circulating.

[0–4 s] Stitch or greenscreen the headline/stat (screenshot is fine). [4–12 s] Antonia reacts: 'Here's what nobody says next.' [12–22 s] The practical bit: screen height, demo. CTA.

## Script skeleton

```
'This is what we do.' [demo]
'DigiRoo. Bio.'
```

2. Antonia to camera, 8 s
3. Demo: slouch → lift, 8 s

## On-screen text pattern
headline screenshot / 'you can't un-screen a kid' / 'but you can move the screen'

# 07 · Three things I didn't know until I became a mom

**Pillar:** A · **Length:** 25–35 s · **Hook type:** Listicle / curiosity gap

**Use when:** You have talking-head energy and no kid available.

## Structure (beats)
[0–2 s] 'Three things nobody told me about kids and screens.' [2–10 s] #1 (relatable, not product). [10–18 s] #2 (relatable). [18–30 s] #3 = screen height; demo. CTA.

## Script skeleton
```
'Three things nobody told me about kids and tablets.'
'One: they will find the iPad. Doesn't matter where you hid it.'
'Two: the volume will always be at 100.'
'Three: the real problem isn't how long, it's how low. Head down, neck down, for an hour.'
'So I made a case that lifts it. DigiRoo. In my bio.'
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Antonia selfie to camera, 3 beats
2. Cutaway for each point (iPad hiding spot, volume, slouch), 3 s each
3. Demo lift, 5 s

## On-screen text pattern
'1' '2' '3' / 'not how long, how low'

## Why it works
Numbered structure holds attention; two non-product beats earn the third.

## How DigiRoo uses it
Keep points 1–2 funny and universal; point 3 is always the product.

# 12 · 'But will my kid actually use it?' (objection kill)

**Pillar:** C · **Length:** 20–30 s · **Hook type:** Direct address / objection

**Use when:** Comments or DMs raise the same doubt (durability, will they use it, does it fit, is it worth $50).

## Structure (beats)
[0–2 s] Read the objection on screen. [2–15 s] Show the answer, don't argue it: drop test, kid carrying it, fits check, 3 months of use. [15–25 s] One honest caveat. CTA.

## Script skeleton
```
'Someone asked: will my kid actually use the stand or just ignore it?'
'Fair. Here's day one.' [kid ignores it]
'Here's week two.' [kid flips it up without being asked]
'Turns out eye level is just comfier. They figure it out.'
'DigiRoo, bio.'
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Screenshot of the comment, 3 s
2. Proof clips, 10 s
3. Antonia caveat to camera, 5 s

## On-screen text pattern
the objection verbatim / 'day 1' 'week 2'

## Why it works
Answers the question the buyer is silently asking; comment screenshots read as social proof.

## How DigiRoo uses it
Keep a running list of objections in lessons-learned.md; one per month becomes this format.

# 15 · Stance carousel (opinion, photo post)

**Pillar:** A · **Length:** 5–7 slides · **Hook type:** Contrarian stance / permission

**Use when:** You have a parenting opinion you'd defend at dinner, a screen-ban story is in the news, or no kid is available to film. TikTok photo mode + IG carousel from the same slides.

## Structure (beats)
[Slide 1] The stance in 8 words or fewer, over a real photo of a kid using the iPad at eye level: 'Screen time is NOT a bad choice.' [Slide 2] The 'because': 'It's a personal choice for your family.' [Slides 3–5] One concrete house rule per slide (no screens at dinner; iPads weekends only; screens come up to eye level). [Slide 6] Where DigiRoo fits, one line, product in the photo. [Last slide] A question parents want to answer.

## Script skeleton
```
1  Screen time is NOT a bad choice.
2  It's a personal choice. Here's what works in our house (10 and 7).
3  Rule 1: no screens at the dinner table.
4  Rule 2: no iPads on school nights.
5  Rule 3: when they do use it, the screen comes up to eye level.
6  That's why I made DigiRoo. (product photo)
7  What's your family's one screen rule? 👇
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Kid using the iPad on the DigiRoo stand at eye level, natural light (cover slide)
2. Dinner table with no devices
3. iPads stacked in a basket / charging drawer
4. Kid upright with the stand raised
5. Product close-up in a real room (not studio)

## On-screen text pattern
Slide 1: one bold line, big type, top third. Other slides: 20 words max, same font and position on every slide.

## Why it works
A stance gives people something to agree with or argue with, and both send it further. Swiping sets its own pace, so people read every slide; on TikTok photo mode it gets pushed to non-followers. It needs no filming day.

## How DigiRoo uses it
One a week while we test (replaces a static graphic). Rotate stances: screen time isn't the enemy; bans backfire; posture over minutes ('It's not just how long, it's how'). Use a trending sound on TikTok. No medical claims (brief §5); the product slide says 'lifts the screen to eye level'.

# 16 · Collab reel (co-posted with a partner)

**Pillar:** D · **Length:** 15–45 s · **Hook type:** Borrowed audience / guest face

**Use when:** A parent creator, school, clinic, event partner or local business will co-post. On Instagram use the Collab invite when posting, so the reel lives on both profiles and the counts merge. On TikTok there's no equivalent: the partner posts and tags @digiroocase, or we stitch them.

## Structure (beats)
[0–2 s] The guest's face and a joint hook: 'I'm Caroline, a pediatric physio, and Antonia asked me one question.' [2–20 s] The guest's bit: their tip, story or event, in their voice. [20–35 s] Antonia (or the product) answers with one thing parents can do; the stand lifts on screen. [35–45 s] The ask: event date, or 'follow us both'.

## Script skeleton
```
GUEST:   'I'm [name], [who they are]. Antonia asked me [question].'
GUEST:   [their answer / tip / event in one breath]
ANTONIA: 'Which is why the screen comes up to eye level in our house.' [stand lifts]
BOTH:    'Follow us both for the next one.' / 'See you on [date].'
```

## Shot list skeleton (phone only)
1. Guest to camera, natural light, their own space, 5–15 s
2. Antonia to camera or a whip-pan between the two, 5 s
3. Kid + DigiRoo stand lifting, 3–5 s
4. Both in frame, or the event card, 3 s

## On-screen text pattern
Word-by-word captions, white boxes, centre. The guest's name and role on screen in the first 2 s.

## Why it works
The partner's followers see it as their own feed content, not an ad, and collab reels count reach from both audiences. A second credible face (clinician, educator, parent creator) carries trust that a solo product post can't.

## How DigiRoo uses it
Plan one a month. Partners in order: Bermuda event/community partners, affiliate clinics (pairs with format 14), parent creators with kids aged 4–12. Get written OK before filming. Clinician collabs get **[REVIEW: clinician]** on the post card, and no clinician endorsement until it's agreed in writing (brief §5). Kids on camera need their parent's written OK.
